TARS4 — wiring guide

The 110 TARS wires (33 in 26 AWG, the rest in 30 AWG), in build order. Each step is tested on the bench before the next; everything is done outside TARS, fitting comes at the end. The board plans (renders/tars4_board_*.svg) give hole by hole, this guide gives both ends of every wire.

Wire end code (the same on the board plans)

●Soldered: on a board hole (plan shown) or on a module pad / lead. Tin the wire, solder, heat-shrink over the joint if it is exposed.
DFDupont, female contact crimped (SN-28B, 30 AWG folded in two; two wires in one contact: together, without folding), slid into housing Xn at the cavity shown (cavity 1 = pin 1, paint dot).
DMDupont, male contact: the module side of an inline pair (pigtails of X3, X7, X15).
XHFJST-XH female crimped, on the power block side (X10, X13, X14) or the cell side (X12).
XHMJST-XH male crimped, the other side of the pair.
Wire colour, thick = 26 AWG, strokes = black heat-shrink rings at both ends (1 = I2S / PIR, 2 = I2C, 3 = microSD).
Power pairs: red / black = battery and 5 V, white / blue = regulated 3V3. Rails sharing red / black carry a coloured band (10 mm of coloured heat-shrink, shrunk 2–3 cm from each end, the same on the + and on its GND): none = cell B+ / B−, white = TP4056 OUT+ / OUT−, yellow = VPATH, orange = VSYS, purple = VUSB. Slip the band on before soldering or crimping.

Diagram blocks (frame colour)

PHand-wired board: P1, P2 (stripboards), P3 S3 carrier, P4 power path (pad perfboards); plans renders/tars4_board_*.svg.
MModule or part under its name: TP4056, TPS63020, INMP441, AM312, microSD reader, switch, cells, speaker…
XDupont connector, one side (female or male); cavities are numbered from pin 1.
XJST-XH connector, one side (female or male).

Steps

  1. 1. Power block, on the bench
  2. 2. Charge port, switch, cells
  3. 3. S3 carrier
  4. 4. P1 and the left middle
  5. 5. Left tube: power block ↔ left middle, microSD
  6. 6. Middle tube and right middle
  7. 7. Right tube and right leg
  8. Lengths
  9. Full list
  10. Connectors

In the diagrams, TARS is seen from the front (left leg on the left), one column per TARS column, the tubes between them. A block = a board, a module or one side of a connector; each line = one wire end. A wire started at one step and finished later leaves the block with an arrow "→ st. n".

1 Power block, on the bench

left leg: TP4056, power-path board, TPS63020 soldered together · 22 wires finished · housings to fill: X10 F, X12 M, X13 F, X14 F, X16 M

Before

  1. Power-path board: parts, bridges and GND bus per renders/tars4_board_power.svg (Q1 / Q5 with wire-wrap wire).
  2. TP4056: R_PROG replaced by 2.4 k, then tested alone: 3.7 V bench supply on B+ / B−, current < 10 µA. Polarities: C9 + on IN+, D3 band (cathode) on IN+ (reversed, it shorts the 5 V). TPS63020: EN tied to VIN, PS/SYNC to GND.
  3. Crowded pads (joints ≥ 0.65 mm from the board end): splice 1 cm before the pad the two VUSB wires of IN+ (to X10 and to the power-path board), the two B+ (to X12 and X16, with the B+ sense wire to the power-path board) and the two B−: a single conductor per pad, next to C9 / D3.
  4. Solder the wires below (4–5 cm loops between the three boards), then crimp the XH contacts and slide them into X10, X12, X13 and X14.
  5. X12 and X16 on the block side (M): while unplugged, capped with an empty female XH housing. Their pins carry B+ / B− as soon as a cell is plugged in, until step 7.

Bench test

  • 3.7 V bench supply on X12 (block side, M): OUT+ ≈ B+; current without USB noted (D1 leakage adds to the TP4056 one: a few tens of µA possible; power_budget.md).
  • X10 cavities 3–4 bridged (switch simulated): VSYS ≈ B+; 3.3 V on X13 cavity 3; VBAT/2 ≈ B+ / 2 on X14 cavity 1.
  • 5 V on X10 cavities 1–2: charge LED, USB_DET ≈ 3 V on X14 cavity 2, Q1 off.

2 Charge port, switch, cells

the foot and cell cables up to X10, X12 and X16 · 6 wires finished · housings to fill: X10 M, X12 F

Before

  1. Solder F1 on the left + plate (F2 on the right one at step 7). Never solder on a cell.
  2. Right cell wires: long enough to cross the three tubes (length from the table, already + 3 cm, offered up on TARS before cutting). Crimp X16 (female) now; the right cell end stays bare.

Bench test

  • Left cell alone: X12 plugged in, switch on, VSYS ≈ B+.
  • Charger on J1: charge LED; unplugged: VUSB < 0.5 V within ~1 s.

3 S3 carrier

the 27 controller wires, soldered on the carrier side · 0 wires finished · housings to fill: none

Before

  1. Plan renders/tars4_board_s3.svg: 2 × 8 headers (V contact removed, headers glued), standing parts, bridges, GND bus, jumpers.
  2. Solder the 27 wires on the carrier side only, long enough (6–8 cm service loop + route). The other end stays bare: it is finished at the step shown.

Bench test

  • Before any power-up: every still-free end capped with closed heat-shrink (shrunk, end pinched while hot).
  • S3 removed: each wire ↔ its pin with the ohmmeter, GND isolated from 3V3 and the signals.
  • S3 plugged in, PC USB: test program flashed, the S3 boots.

4 P1 and the left middle

screen 1, mic, accelerometer · 29 wires finished · housings to fill: X1 F, X2 F, X3 F, X3 M

Before

  1. Plan renders/tars4_board_p1.svg. 1 × 8 right-angle header on the back of screen 1 (X1). ADXL345: straight header, INT2 removed and its cavity plugged (X2).
  2. INMP441: 5-wire pigtail (male contacts, X3); L/R bridged to GND on its board.
  3. X2 SDA and SCL: double contact, crimp together (without folding back) the S3 wire and the one leaving for P2 (bare end, soldered at step 6).

Bench test

  • Before any power-up: every still-free end capped with closed heat-shrink (shrunk, end pinched while hot).
  • S3 on USB, switch off: screen 1 displays, the mic gives I2S samples, the ADXL345 answers at 0x53 and INT1 toggles.

5 Left tube: power block ↔ left middle, microSD

everything crossing the left tube · 15 wires finished · housings to fill: X13 M, X14 M, X15 F, X15 M

Before

  1. Thread the left brass tube onto the listed wires BEFORE crimping the far end. The amplifier pair (step 6) and the right cell pair (step 2) also cross this tube: thread them at the same time.
  2. microSD reader: C4 10 µF tantalum lying flat (+ on VCC; only ~6.6 mm up to the TPS63020) and C5 100 nF on its VCC / GND pins; without pull-ups on the reader, R5–R9 10 k from CMD, D0, D1, D2 and D3 to VCC (SD_3V3). Then a 5-wire pigtail (male contacts, X15).

Bench test

  • Before any power-up: every still-free end capped with closed heat-shrink (shrunk, end pinched while hot).
  • Without USB, switch on: the S3 boots from the cells (3.3 V on the carrier).
  • VBAT/2 and USB_DET read by the S3; the microSD is read; SD_EN high cuts its 3.3 V.

6 Middle tube and right middle

screen 2, amplifier, speaker, AM312, P2 · 28 wires finished · housings to fill: X2 F, X4 F, X5 F, X6 F, X7 F, X7 M, X13 M

Before

  1. Plan renders/tars4_board_p2.svg. Right-angle header on the back of screen 2 (X4). Amplifier: 1 × 4 (GAIN removed) + 1 × 3 headers (X5), 2-pin header instead of the screw terminal (X6), C7 + on VIN, band (−) to GND.
  2. AM312: 3-wire pigtail (male contacts, X7), breakout pins trimmed flush, breakout slipped into a heat-shrink sock (it passes 5 mm from the middle tube exit). Thread the middle tube before crimping.

7 Right tube and right leg

DS3231, BME280, right cell · 10 wires finished · housings to fill: X8 F, X9 F, X16 F

Before

  1. DS3231: right-angle header, 32K removed, coin-cell charging resistor removed. BME280: 1 × 4 header, LED removed.
  2. Thread the right tube. F2 on the right + plate, then solder the two right cell wires (step 2).
  3. X9: each contact takes two wires (P2 + the continuation to X8), crimped together without folding back.
  4. Right tube: twist SDA with GND and SCL with 3V3 (long I2C bus, next to SCK / BCLK).

Bench test

  • I2C scan: 0x53 (ADXL345), 0x57 (DS3231 EEPROM), 0x68 (DS3231), 0x76 or 0x77 (BME280).
  • Before plugging in the right cell (X16): same voltage as the left one within 0.05 V.
